history.alt_text: A heavy-duty power meter block and a tiny standard wall adapter rendered in matte clay on a concrete surface.
history.caption: Hunting down tiny half-watt wall adapters ignores the heavy standby loads hiding in larger household gear.
history.title: Standby-Power-Vampires

style_when: the news is structural and abstract — a stack reordered, a layer added, a flow rerouted — and there is no literal object that carries it, so the idea is stated as a small physical assembly of recognisable parts rather than as bare shapes
prompt: Matte clay 3D render of a heavy-duty power meter block bridging a thick conduit cable, dwarfing a tiny standard wall adapter placed beside it, extreme asymmetry with heavy off-centre weighting. The modular electrical assembly rests on a weathered concrete floor in a garage. One strong directional key light raking from the right throws long cast shadows across the concrete. Matte surfaces with visible moulding seams, rendered in graphite, bone white, and a subtle accent of rust. Generous negative space, no legible text, no embossed lettering.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, plain spheres, simple cubes, floating geometric shapes, glossy reflections
rationale: The clay render allows us to abstract the concept of standby load size into a physical, architectural assembly of recognizable electrical parts—a massive meter block and a tiny adapter—without getting bogged down in literal brand specifics or cluttered environments.
cue: Your standby bill hides about 62 watts
subject: a heavy-duty power meter block dwarfing a tiny standard wall adapter
core_thesis: The continuous standby power load in households is driven by large appliances drawing heavy watts, making the traditional advice of unplugging tiny half-watt chargers economically pointless.
core_conflict: trivial perceived savings vs hidden high-wattage appliance loads
composition: extreme asymmetry with heavy off-centre weighting
alt_text: The 62 Watt Standby Load. A heavy molded plug and braided cord beside a small wall adapter, rendered in matte clay on cracked concrete.
caption: The 62 Watt Standby Load: The hidden appliances driving your idle electricity bill.
title: The 62 Watt Standby Load

review.depicts: A large, blocky power meter device with thick braided cables sits on a cracked surface next to a small standard wall adapter.
review.reason: The image shows a power meter and a wall adapter, which relates to the article's focus on measuring standby power draw.
